## Quality Guardrails (faq rubric)

Self-evaluate against every category below before reporting done; revise until the pass criteria hold.

- [ ] **Working Backwards Fidelity** (required): Whether the FAQ genuinely vets the product idea rather than just marketing it
  - FAQ challenges the Press Release; surfaces real concerns; feels like honest vetting
- [ ] **Question Coverage** (required, blocking): Whether the FAQ anticipates the questions customers will actually ask, and answers the canonical vetting set: what problem are we solving, what will customers care most about, what would disappoint them most at launch, what will they love most
  - Comprehensive coverage including tough questions customers and stakeholders will ask
- [ ] **Answer Clarity** (required): How clearly and directly questions are answered
  - Direct, clear answers with no evasion; honest about limitations
- [ ] **Self-Critical Honesty** (required): Earn Trust: whether the document is vocally self-critical about limitations and risks
  - Honest about what the product can't do; acknowledges risks and limitations; earns trust
- [ ] **Objection Handling** (required): Whether the FAQ addresses likely concerns with honest, substantive responses
  - Proactively addresses concerns with honest, confident responses; disagree-and-commit spirit
- [ ] **Customer Language** (required): Whether questions and answers use customer language, not internal jargon
  - Questions phrased as customers would ask; answers in plain language
- [ ] **Pricing Transparency** (advisory): Clarity of pricing and cost-related information
  - Clear pricing with examples and cost estimation guidance
- [ ] **Getting Started Clarity** (required): How well the path to adoption is explained
  - Clear step-by-step path from interest to success; bias for action
- [ ] **Disconfirmation Rigor** (required): Are Right, A Lot / Earn Trust: the FAQ works to disconfirm the press release's claims — diverse perspectives, vocally self-critical — rather than defending the proposal
  - Hard questions genuinely attack the proposal's core claims; at least one answer concedes a real weakness or open risk; competitor and customer counter-perspectives are named

Overall pass: every required category passes; findings allowed: 0 critical, 0 high, 0 medium, unlimited low
